title: Human-in-the-Loop & Agent Guardrails
subtitle: The badge worked, and now your manager is drowning. A second reader, a confidence dial, and how to ask a person well.
heroTitle: Human-in-the-Loop & Agent Guardrails

objectives.title: Feel Why "A Person Approves It" Isn't Enough
objectives.description: Play the manager with 30 approvals and 75 seconds, see what you let through, and connect it to a real case of rubber-stamping.

objectives.title: Add a Second Reader
objectives.description: Use a second AI call that never writes: it reads each answer and says, 0 to 100, how sure it is that the answer can go out with nobody looking.

objectives.title: Set a Confidence Threshold
objectives.description: Pick the bar yourself. Below it a person reads the answer first. Score your choice against an answer key: handled alone, right call, wasted, slipped.

objectives.title: Decide What Always Goes to a Person
objectives.description: Add always-ask rules for the things you'd never leave to a score, and design an approval a person can judge in ten seconds.

agenda.title: 🟢 Rubber Stamp, Round 1
agenda.description: Friday, 4:30 PM. You're the manager. 30 drafts wait for your OK. 75 seconds.
bulletPoints: Last week's badge: zero incidents, and 150 × 3 minutes = 7.5 hours of the manager's day
Play on your phone, then hands up: who approved a bad one?
Rubber-stamping: the smoke alarm that goes off every time you make toast

agenda.title: Cold Open: Four Real Cases
agenda.description: One question per story, shouted out before the reveal.
bulletPoints: Uber, 2022: a contractor flooded with approval prompts says yes to one
New York City's business chatbot, 2024: polite, confident, and describing how to break the law
Cursor's support bot "Sam", 2025: invents a policy instead of saying "I'm not sure"
Klarna, 2024 → 2025: from "the work of 700 agents" to hiring people again

agenda.title: A Badge That Knows When to Ask + Round 2
agenda.description: Three upgrades, then the same tray again.
bulletPoints: 🧑‍⚖️ The second reader: an editor, not a spell-checker
🎚️ The dial: a confidence threshold you set. Too low, something slips. Too high, the manager drowns
📌 Always ask: what goes to a person however sure the AI is
Rubber Stamp, round 2: 24 drafts went out on their own, 6 reach you with reasons. And one that shouldn't have

agenda.title: Hands-On: The Dial, Parts 1–4
agenda.description: Same company as last week, a bigger inbox, and an answer key.
bulletPoints: Part 2: 8 messages with last week's badge. Bet how many really need a person
Part 3: the second reader scores every answer
Part 4: drag the live dial. Gut first, then reveal the answer key. Goal: zero slipped, as few wasted as you can
Class tally on the board: same model, why different bars?

agenda.title: 🎬 Render Desk: Make a Real AI Video
agenda.description: Teams of two ask a real approver for a real render.
bulletPoints: A Director agent writes your video prompt and your approval card. You fix the card and send it
Seedance 2.5, 4 to 10 seconds, with sound, rendered on the professor's account, only if the approver says yes
Decide in ten seconds: the approver reads your card on the screen and approves, sends it back, or declines

agenda.title: Premiere + Homework
agenda.description: Every approved video on the big screen.
bulletPoints: HW #9 Final Project Pitch due Thu Nov 19: do Parts 5 and 6 of The Dial at home and paste Part 6's blue box into your guardrail sentence
Wednesday: when the trap hides in a document your agent reads, and what your agent costs

agenda.title: Cold Open: Two Songs, One Person
agenda.description: The same AI made both. Which one is really for them?
bulletPoints: Song one came from one lazy sentence
Song two came from five true details
Same AI. What changed?

agenda.title: 🎵 A Song for Someone: Three Takes
agenda.description: Pick one person who matters to you. Make them a song in Suno.
bulletPoints: Take 1, the lazy one: tell the AI who it's for and nothing else
Take 2, the true one: add five true things only you know
Take 3, the director's cut: choose the sound, the mood, the voice and the language
Rather make something wild? Go for it. Any song, any style, about anything

agenda.title: Send It
agenda.description: Text the song to them now, before you talk yourself out of it.
bulletPoints: Open your best take in Suno and press Share
Then tell us what they said

agenda.title: The Premiere
agenda.description: Volunteers only. Tell us who it's for, then play one minute.
bulletPoints: If they wrote back, read it to us
The room votes: Goosebumps, Biggest Laugh, Best Detail, Best Reply

agenda.title: What You Just Learned
agenda.description: Three words for what you did today.
bulletPoints: Context: the AI had the music, you had the details
Iteration: your third take beat your first
Judgment: Suno made six songs, you chose one

activities.title: The Dial
activities.description: About 20 minutes in the notebook, Parts 1 to 4:

steps.title: The tray is full (5 min)
steps.description: Your AI employee answers 8 messages. With last week's badge, every answer to an outside person waits for the manager. Bet: how many of the 8 really need a person?

steps.title: Hire a second reader (5 min)
steps.description: A second AI call that never writes. It reads each answer and scores it 0 to 100: how sure is it that this can go out with nobody looking?

steps.title: Set your dial (9 min)
steps.description: Drag the live dial and watch the messages move between "goes out alone" and "waits for the manager". Reveal the answer key: ✅ handled alone, 🟡 right call, 🥱 wasted, 😬 slipped. Aim for zero slipped and as few wasted as you can, then lock in your bar and write why.

steps.title: Talk to the Director
steps.description: An AI agent on your class pass. Tell it your company and the feeling. It drafts a 4 to 10 second video prompt and the approval card.

steps.title: Fix the card and send it
steps.description: Who's asking, what it shows, can it be undone, why it's safe, and what the approver should check. Make it a ten-second yes. Then watch your screen.

steps.title: Upload it
steps.description: When your video is done, download it from the Render Desk and upload it to the class folder (link in Resources), named with your team name.

activities.title: A Song for Someone
activities.description: Wednesday, about 40 minutes, on your own or with a partner:

steps.title: Take 1: the lazy one
steps.description: Tell Suno who the song is for and nothing else. Listen. Nice song, but it could be for anyone.

steps.title: Take 2: the true one
steps.description: Add five true things only you know: something they always say, a food, a place, a habit, one small memory. Listen again. What changed?

steps.title: Take 3: the director's cut
steps.description: Now direct the band. Choose the sound, the mood, the voice and the language. Change one thing and go again.

steps.title: Send it
steps.description: Share your best take with them before class ends. Then tell us what they said.

takeaways.text: A human in the loop is not a guardrail. A human who is paying attention is. Send a person 150 approvals a day and you get a rubber stamp. Send fewer, better questions.
The dial is a business decision. Set the bar too low and something slips out that needed a person. Too high and your manager reads everything again. The AI doesn't pick the bar. You do.
Tone is not risk, and friendly is not safe. A word list reads words. A second reader reads meaning. It can still be confidently wrong, which is what always-ask rules are for.
Rules for what you already know. A second reader for what you don't. A person for what matters. And when you ask a person, show them who is asking, what will happen, and whether it can be undone.
The AI had the music. You had the details. Take 1 was for anyone. Take 2 was for one person. The only thing that changed was what you told it. In AI, we call that context.
